source_span: Checking $6$, we find that $6\cdot 7=42$, so our list becomes $$1\quad 2 \quad 3 \quad 6 \quad \underline{\hphantom{10}} \quad \dots \quad \underline{\hphantom{10}} \quad 7 \quad 14 \quad 21 \quad 42.$$  Since $7$ is already on our list, our final list is $$1\quad 2 \quad 3 \quad 6 \quad 7 \quad 14 \quad 21 \quad 42.$$  We compare our lists for the factors of $14$ and the factors of $42$ to see that the factors that $14$ and $42$ share are $1$, $2$, $7$, and $14$.
